final_answer: Adopt the full-frame YOLO DETECTION paradigm (K-01) as the keystone that resolves the entire dataset-export class: the first model trains on FULL event frames with class+bbox labels normalized to full-frame dimensions, and crops are demoted to human/VLM review artifacts that never enter the training set. On top of that, build two enforcement keystones — ONE reusable dataset-invariant validator (K-02) and ONE mandatory finetune-gate orchestrator (K-03/D-FG-03) whose definition-of-done is a passing CI integration test, NOT a commit message (this is precisely how 99034ac5 was falsely marked done). Every behavior-changing fix lands red-first (a test that fails on current HEAD and reproduces the bug) before the minimal fix and an architect review of the (test, fix) pair (K-04, relaxed so trivial structural atoms get lightweight, non-blocking review). All 17 remaining bugs are accepted as fixes across clusters A (FRAME-SYNC: crop from the detection's own immutable event frame, bbox bound to that exact frame, buffer protected from mutation), B (CROP-NAMING: non-resetting + camera_id + per-detection name components, strict image<->label stem pairing, atomic writes), C (DATASET-EXPORT: full-frame normalization, image/label atomicity, empty labels for negatives, persisted frame_w/h, K-02 pre-training validation), D (FINETUNE-GATE: detection-metric eval via model.val() not .probs, name-based class identity, the orchestrator), and E (MISLABEL: track-bound labels, VLM-disagreement quarantine). The single high-impact conflict — K-01 vs C-DE-01 — is resolved in K-01's favor: C-DE-01 is narrowed to full-frame normalization only, with at most an inactive interface seam for a future crop path. Cluster E is folded into the green-gate (K-05) at least as a quarantine. No atom was rejected outright; the judge accepted 21 and modified 2 (K-04, C-DE-01). The first training is hard-blocked by the K-03 orchestrator until clusters A-D (and E per K-05) are verified green via pytest in CI.

decisions.decision: K-01 KEYSTONE: First model is a YOLO DETECTION finetune trained on FULL event frames; labels are class+bbox normalized to full-frame dimensions; crops become human/VLM review artifacts only, never training images.
decisions.rationale: Eliminates the crop-vs-full-frame label ambiguity that is the root cause of the entire C cluster, preserves scene context, and yields a single unambiguous export contract. Judge accept 0.845.
alternatives_considered: Train on crops with crop-local labels (rejected: context loss plus coordinate ambiguity)
Support both crop and full-frame training simultaneously now (deferred: premature complexity for the first model)
decisions.risk: Larger/slower images; if frame_w/h is wrong every label is wrong - mitigated by C-DE-04 (persist dims) and the K-02 validator.
decisions.test: Exporter writes a full-frame image whose dimensions match the recorded frame_w/h and a label whose de-normalized bbox lands on the object (IoU>0.9 with the known box).

decisions.decision: K-02 KEYSTONE: Build ONE reusable dataset-invariant validator encoding every YOLO export rule (1:1 image<->label, background -> empty label file, all coords in [0,1], every class id is a known data.yaml name, frame_w/h present and used for normalization).
decisions.rationale: Central control for dataset integrity; becomes the shared test harness for all C atoms and is invoked by the K-03 orchestrator. Judge accept 0.88.
alternatives_considered: Ad-hoc per-atom checks (rejected: duplication and drift)
decisions.risk: A validator bug gives false confidence - mitigated by shipping it with its own positive/negative fixtures.
decisions.test: The validator has positive/negative fixtures proving it fails dirty datasets and passes clean ones; it is itself the harness for all C atoms.

decisions.decision: K-03 KEYSTONE: The finetune-gate ORCHESTRATOR is the single enforcer of 'no training until A-D green': it runs (1) the K-02 validator and (2) a real detection-mAP eval via model.val() on a FIXED held-out fixture, and ABORTS training with a human-readable reason on any red. Definition-of-done is the orchestrator's integration test passing in CI, not a commit message.
decisions.rationale: Makes validation + detection eval a hard precondition and directly fixes the '99034ac5 marked done but broken' failure mode by binding DoD to a passing test. Judge accept 0.8125.
alternatives_considered: Trust commit messages / a manual checklist (rejected: exactly what failed before)
decisions.risk: CI cost and fixture management; model.val() runtime - mitigated by a tiny fixed fixture and a small model.
decisions.test: Red dataset OR sub-threshold metric -> training refused; both green -> training proceeds.

decisions.decision: K-04 (MODIFIED) KEYSTONE: Default to DISCUSS-First + red-first TDD for behavior-changing atoms (clusters A, C, D, E and B-CN-01/03/05): land a test that FAILS on current HEAD reproducing the documented failure, then the minimal fix to green, then architect reviews the (test, fix) pair before merge. For purely structural/low-risk atoms (B-CN-02 camera-id, B-CN-04 stem-pairing) red-first is recommended and review is lightweight and non-blocking.
decisions.rationale: Red-first proves both the bug and the fix; relaxing the blocking requirement for trivial atoms avoids process overhead. Judge modify 0.7475 (overbroad_process_requirement -0.05).
alternatives_considered: Mandatory blocking architect review on every atom incl. trivial ones (rejected: too rigid)
No red-first requirement (rejected: cannot prove regressions are actually caught)
decisions.risk: Mis-classifying a behavior-changing atom as 'structural' could skip needed scrutiny - when in doubt, treat as behavior-changing.
decisions.test: Each behavior-changing atom's test is demonstrated red on the pre-fix commit and green after the fix.

decisions.decision: K-05 KEYSTONE: Fold cluster E (#13/#14) into the green-gate, or at minimum quarantine VLM-disagreements and track-less triggers out of the training set, even though the literal constraint names only A-D.
decisions.rationale: Mislabeled positives poison training as badly as the A-D bugs; cheap insurance against a known hole. Judge accept 0.7775.
alternatives_considered: Strictly limit the gate to A-D (rejected: leaves a known mislabel hole open before first training)
decisions.risk: Over-aggressive quarantine shrinks the dataset - mitigate by quarantining/logging for review rather than silently dropping.
decisions.test: Gate fails or sample is excluded when detector class_name disagrees with the VLM verdict, or when a trigger lacks a track_id.

decisions.decision: A-FS-01 FRAME-SYNC: Crop and label from the detection's own immutable event frame (identified by an explicit index), not the latest buffered frame and not pending.frames[0] unconditionally (use the event index when a pre-event buffer exists).
decisions.rationale: Fixes #1/#2/#12 - cropping a frame captured ~11s after the event produces background under the person/cat label. Judge accept 0.875.
alternatives_considered: Always use frames[0] (rejected: wrong when a pre-event buffer exists)
Use the latest frame (rejected: this is the original bug)
decisions.risk: Requires the true event-frame index to be known - see open question on the pending.frames buffer layout.
decisions.test: Simulate a detection event with object movement; assert the crop's pixels match the event-frame object region and the source index used is the event frame (not latest, not frames[0] when a pre-event buffer is present).

decisions.decision: A-FS-02 FRAME-SYNC: Bind the bbox to the exact source frame the crop is cut from; never recompute the bbox against later frames; apply this pairing to ALL crop-collection paths (primary and secondary).
decisions.rationale: Prevents subtle temporal misalignment between box coordinates and pixels across both code paths. Judge accept 0.8625.
alternatives_considered: Fix only the primary path (rejected: the secondary path leaks the same bug)
decisions.risk: The secondary path may have different plumbing - verify the same temporal alignment analogously.
decisions.test: For both primary and secondary paths, simulate object movement between frames and assert the crop uses the original bbox and pixels from the same source frame.

decisions.decision: A-FS-03 FRAME-SYNC: Make the selected event frame immutable and protect pending.frames from mutation or dequeue reordering until the crop is successfully recorded.
decisions.rationale: Hardens against post-trigger buffer mutation/reorder bugs with a clear testable invariant. Judge accept 0.81.
alternatives_considered: Copy only the chosen frame at trigger time (acceptable alternative implementation)
decisions.risk: Memory cost of retaining a frame - bounded by retaining a single frame copy.
decisions.test: Simulate new frames added to pending.frames after a trigger; assert the crop remains unchanged and is taken from the originally selected immutable event frame.

decisions.decision: B-CN-01 CROP-NAMING: Naming scheme includes a non-resetting component (run UUID, UTC timestamp, or persistent monotonic counter) so a frame_id reset on process restart cannot overwrite prior samples.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #3/#7 - frame_id resets to 0 on restart and overwrites earlier crops. Judge accept 0.87.
alternatives_considered: frame_id only (rejected: resets to 0 on restart)
decisions.risk: Sub-millisecond timestamp collisions - combine timestamp with a counter or UUID.
decisions.test: Simulate a restart resetting frame_id to 0; emit a crop with a previously used frame_id; assert the pre-existing and new crops coexist with distinct names.

decisions.decision: B-CN-02 CROP-NAMING: Include camera_id/source_id in the crop/image/label naming scheme to prevent collisions between cameras that share frame_ids.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #8 inter-camera collision; very low cost. Judge accept 0.8975.
decisions.risk: camera_id/source_id must be available at export time - see open question.
decisions.test: Two cameras emit samples with the same frame_id; assert distinct filenames and preserved image/label pairs without conflict.

decisions.decision: B-CN-03 CROP-NAMING: Include a per-detection/track index (track_id, event_id, or monotonic suffix) so multiple detections within one frame get unique names.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #15 intra-frame multi-detection overwrite. Judge accept 0.855.
decisions.risk: track_id may be absent for track-less triggers - fall back to a monotonic suffix (ties to E-ML-01).
decisions.test: Simulate a single frame with two or more distinct detections; assert two or more distinct sample names, one per detection.

decisions.decision: B-CN-04 CROP-NAMING: Derive the label sidecar filename from the exact same composite key as its image, maintaining strict image<->label stem pairing under the new scheme.
decisions.rationale: Guarantees the 1:1 pairing the K-02 validator enforces; highest judge score 0.9175.
decisions.risk: Low.
decisions.test: For every exported image assert exactly one matching label file with an aligned stem, and vice-versa.

decisions.decision: B-CN-05 CROP-NAMING: Use atomic write operations for crop images and labels (write-to-temp-then-rename, or fail-on-existing destination) to prevent silent overwrites or partial writes.
decisions.rationale: Protects against concurrent export and partial-file states. Judge accept 0.825.
alternatives_considered: Plain overwrite (rejected: silent data loss)
decisions.risk: Cross-platform rename semantics on Windows - use os.replace or an equivalent atomic rename.
decisions.test: Two concurrent export processes write samples with identical source IDs; assert the operation either fails explicitly or yields distinct, non-overwriting files.

decisions.decision: C-DE-01 (MODIFIED) DATASET-EXPORT: Normalize YOLO label coordinates to FULL-FRAME dimensions for all training exports (full frames only, per K-01). Crop-local normalization is NOT implemented or active for the first model; optionally retain an inactive interface seam for a future crop path, but no crop training path is wired or tested now.
decisions.rationale: Resolves the K-01 conflict: keep the correct full-frame normalization, drop the premature crop-training branch. Judge modify 0.7475 (blocking_conflict_with_K-01 -0.15); micro-debate resolved to full-frame-only for the first model.
alternatives_considered: Implement and test both crop-local and full-frame branches now (rejected/deferred: premature complexity per micro-debate)
decisions.risk: A latent crop branch left in code could be mis-activated - guard it off and mark not-for-training.
decisions.test: De-normalize the exported label against the exported full-frame image's actual dimensions; assert IoU>0.9 with the known ground-truth box.

decisions.decision: C-DE-02 DATASET-EXPORT: Guarantee image/label atomicity - write a label only after its image is successfully saved, and prevent or prune orphan labels (labels without a matching image).
decisions.rationale: Fixes #5 orphan labels and aligns with the K-02 'every label has an image' invariant. Judge accept 0.86.
decisions.risk: Partial failure mid-export - write ordering plus cleanup handles it.
decisions.test: Simulate an image-write failure or a missing source image; assert no dangling label is emitted and the K-02 'every label has an image' invariant holds.

decisions.decision: C-DE-03 DATASET-EXPORT: Background/negative samples never produce a positive bbox - they yield an empty label file (zero rows) or no label, per the YOLO negative-example convention.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #6 - background samples currently emit a positive bbox. Judge accept 0.8875.
alternatives_considered: Skip background entirely (acceptable but loses hard negatives)
decisions.risk: Low.
decisions.test: Export a designated background sample; assert it yields a label file that exists with zero bbox rows.

decisions.decision: C-DE-04 DATASET-EXPORT: Persist original frame_w/h (and crop_w/h if applicable) in the sample manifest/export metadata, and use these as the normalization denominator for bbox coordinates and for validation.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #16/#17 - frame_w/h is lost, breaking normalization. Judge accept 0.89.
alternatives_considered: Infer dimensions from the image at export (rejected: fragile if image is missing or resized)
decisions.risk: Low.
decisions.test: For known frame dimensions and pixel bboxes, assert the export roundtrip preserves the dimensions and the normalized values are exact.

decisions.decision: C-DE-05 DATASET-EXPORT: Run the K-02 validator as a pre-training gate enforcing consistent image/label pairs, coords in [0,1], valid class ids (in data.yaml), and empty labels for background samples.
decisions.rationale: A concrete application of K-02 immediately before training and inside the K-03 orchestrator. Judge accept 0.875.
decisions.risk: Must run on the actual export directory that feeds training, not a sample.
decisions.test: The validator catches and rejects datasets with orphan image/label pairs, out-of-range coordinates, and unknown class ids.

decisions.decision: D-FG-01 FINETUNE-GATE: Evaluate detection outputs (results.boxes with confidence/class) via a detection metric (mAP from model.val()), never classification .probs.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #9 - .probs is empty/meaningless on detection models, the core reason the gate did not work. Judge accept 0.845.
alternatives_considered: Keep using .probs (rejected: the broken behavior)
decisions.risk: model.val() needs a proper data.yaml and held-out fixture.
decisions.test: Feed a detection Results object (boxes, no .probs); assert a detection metric is computed without touching .probs, and known-good vs known-bad models yield distinctly different scores.

decisions.decision: D-FG-02 FINETUNE-GATE: Canonicalize class identity by name, not numeric index - use a single name<->id mapping (from data.yaml) for all gate comparisons.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #10 - numeric index comparisons break under id reordering. Judge accept 0.8675.
alternatives_considered: Compare numeric ids (rejected: fragile to class-id reordering)
decisions.risk: Low.
decisions.test: Simulate a shuffled class-id ordering; assert the gate still matches by name and a genuinely mismatched mapping is detected as red.

decisions.decision: D-FG-03 FINETUNE-GATE: Implement the mandatory finetune orchestrator (the K-03 keystone realized in cluster D) as the single training entry point that sequences the K-02 validator and detection mAP eval and hard-blocks launch with a clear reason if any A-D check is red. This is the SAME artifact as K-03 - one orchestrator, not two.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #11 - without an orchestrator the gate cannot protect anything. Judge accept 0.8125 (intentional duplicate of K-03 tracked in cluster D).
alternatives_considered: Validator and eval as independent optional scripts (rejected: no enforcement)
decisions.risk: High implementation cost - share code with K-03 rather than build a second orchestrator.
decisions.test: Integration test: a red dataset or a sub-threshold model -> training refused with a clear reason; a green dataset + good model -> training allowed.

decisions.decision: E-ML-01 MISLABEL: trigger_detection binds the training label to a specific track_id (or event-detection instance) rather than relying solely on detection category.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #13 - same-category objects get swapped/misattributed without a track binding. Judge accept 0.8525.
alternatives_considered: Category-only binding (rejected: ambiguous with multiple same-class objects)
decisions.risk: Track-less triggers - quarantine them (ties to K-05 and the B-CN-03 monotonic fallback).
decisions.test: Simulate a frame with two same-category objects; assert the label binds to the triggering track_id and is not swapped to the other detection.

decisions.decision: E-ML-02 MISLABEL: Introduce a VLM verification step reconciling the detector class_name with the VLM verdict; on disagreement the sample is dropped/quarantined for review, not auto-labeled with the detector's class.
decisions.rationale: Fixes #14 - detector/VLM mismatch silently poisons labels. Judge accept 0.7525 (higher cost due to VLM reliability/latency/determinism).
alternatives_considered: Trust the detector label (rejected: mislabels)
Trust the VLM label (rejected: VLM also errs - disagreement -> quarantine is the safe rule)
decisions.risk: VLM latency/nondeterminism - the regression test must mock/stub the VLM with fixed verdicts for determinism (open question).
decisions.test: Simulate detector class_name=person but VLM=cat; assert the sample is excluded/flagged and does not enter the positive training set under the detector's label.

rejected.decision: Use crops with crop-local coordinates as training images (the crop-training conditional branch originally in C-DE-01).
rejected.why: Blocking conflict with keystone K-01, which demotes crops to human/VLM review artifacts that are never training images. The micro-debate resolved to full-frame-only for the first model; crop-based training is deferred behind an inactive interface seam, not implemented or tested now.

rejected.decision: Require red-first tests AND merge-blocking architect review for EVERY atom, including purely structural/duplicate ones (K-04 as originally stated).
rejected.why: Overbroad process requirement (judge penalty -0.05). Relaxed: red-first plus blocking review is the default for behavior-changing atoms only; trivial structural atoms (e.g., B-CN-02 camera-id, B-CN-04 stem-pairing) get lightweight, non-blocking review.

rejected.decision: Reject any of the 17 bug-fix atoms outright.
rejected.why: Not applicable - the judge accepted 21 atoms and modified 2 (K-04, C-DE-01); the lowest total score was 0.7475, above the rejection bar. No fix atom was dropped; the two modifications only trimmed sub-clauses.

open_questions: What mAP threshold and held-out fixture composition (size, class balance, source) define 'green' for the K-03 orchestrator's detection evaluation?
Does pending.frames contain a pre-event buffer, and what is the explicit index of the true event frame that A-FS-01 must select?
Is camera_id/source_id available at crop-export time, and in which field, so B-CN-02 can include it in names?
Which VLM backs E-ML-02, and how is its regression test made deterministic (mock/stub with fixed verdicts, fixed seeds)?
For the first training, is cluster E a HARD gate or a soft quarantine? K-05 permits either - the choice must be made before training launches.
What is the CI runtime/cost budget for running model.val() inside the orchestrator integration test - is a tiny fixture model plus a handful of held-out images acceptable?
Are track-less triggers dropped, quarantined, or labeled with a monotonic fallback id (E-ML-01 / B-CN-03 interaction)?

implementation_plan.actions: Establish the red-first TDD default (test fails on HEAD reproducing the bug, then minimal fix, then architect review of the test+fix pair for behavior-changing atoms). Build the ONE dataset-invariant validator with positive and negative fixtures.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: Validator passes clean fixtures and fails every dirty fixture; it is wired into CI as the shared harness for cluster C and the orchestrator.

implementation_plan.actions: Crop/label from the detection's own immutable event frame by explicit index; bind bbox to that exact frame on all crop paths; make the event frame immutable and protect pending.frames from mutation/reorder.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: Movement-based regression tests green on both crop paths; event-frame immutability test green.

implementation_plan.actions: Add non-resetting + camera_id + per-detection components to the naming scheme; derive label stems from the same composite key; use atomic writes.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: Restart, multi-camera, and multi-detection collisions are impossible; strict image<->label stem pairing holds; concurrent writes do not silently overwrite.

implementation_plan.actions: Normalize labels to full-frame dimensions only; enforce image/label atomicity and prune orphans; emit empty labels for background; persist frame_w/h and use them as the normalization denominator; run K-02 on the real export directory.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: K-02 validator passes on a real export; IoU>0.9 label test green; no orphan labels; background -> empty label; dimensions persisted and used.

implementation_plan.actions: Evaluate via detection boxes + mAP (model.val()), never .probs; canonicalize class identity by name from data.yaml; build the single mandatory orchestrator that runs K-02 + detection eval and hard-blocks training on any red with a clear reason.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: Orchestrator integration test green in CI - refuses a red dataset/sub-threshold model with a reason and allows a green dataset + good model. Definition-of-done is this passing test, not a commit message.

implementation_plan.phase: Phase 5 - Cluster E MISLABEL + K-05 wiring
implementation_plan.actions: Bind labels to a concrete track_id/event instance; add VLM reconciliation that quarantines detector/VLM disagreements and track-less triggers; wire these checks into the green-gate.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: Track-bound labels prevent same-class swaps; gate fails or sample is quarantined on VLM disagreement or missing track_id (VLM mocked for determinism).

implementation_plan.phase: Phase 6 - Green-gate verification & first training authorization
implementation_plan.actions: Run the full pytest suite for project oko; confirm the orchestrator is green across clusters A-D (and E per K-05); obtain architect sign-off on all (test, fix) pairs.
implementation_plan.exit_criteria: All cluster gates green and orchestrator integration test passing -> first training is authorized; until then the orchestrator hard-blocks any training launch.

next_step: Implement the K-02 dataset-invariant validator together with its positive/negative fixtures (red-first), since it is the shared test harness for every cluster-C atom and a hard dependency of the K-03/D-FG-03 orchestrator that gates the first training.

red_team_findings.what: K-01's pivot to full-frame training images introduces a partial-annotation defect that no atom handles. trigger_detection emits only the triggering object's bbox, but a full event frame can contain other objects (the untriggered cat next to the triggered person). Those become unlabeled regions in a positive training image, teaching the detector to SUPPRESS true positives.
red_team_findings.why: The export is never specified to aggregate ALL detections in a frame into one multi-row label; C-DE-01's success test asserts IoU>0.9 with 'the known box' (singular) and B-CN-03 keeps one-sample-per-detection naming, both baking in a one-box-per-image assumption. So even after all 23 atoms go green, the first model trains on systematically incomplete labels — success criteria met, goal (a correct training pipeline) not met. This is a NEW, training-corrupting bug created by the keystone itself, arguably worse than the crop-coordinate bugs it replaces.

red_team_findings.what: The mandatory blocking gate is defined over clusters A-D only, but under K-01 cluster E directly determines training-label CORRECTNESS. The full-frame image's class label comes straight from trigger_detection; if E-ML-01 (track_id binding) is wrong, the full-frame training image carries the wrong class (#13). Yet K-05 makes E a 'soft, non-blocking' exclusion, so the first training is permitted to start with E not green.
red_team_findings.why: This lets demonstrably mislabeled samples into the positive training set while the gate reports 'green', violating the stated goal of a correct pipeline before training. The decision even files the E-blocking policy as an unresolved open question (K-05 ratification), so the boundary that allows training to proceed is itself undecided — a critical-risk gate resting on an open question.

red_team_findings.what: The K-03/D-FG-03 gate is described as a PRE-training abort that runs 'a real detection-mAP eval via model.val()'. But model.val() needs a trained model; you cannot compute the finetuned model's mAP before you train it.
red_team_findings.why: As a pre-training gate the mAP arm can only evaluate the base/pretrained checkpoint, which says nothing about the new dataset or the finetune outcome — so it cannot 'prevent bad training' as claimed. mAP eval is inherently a POST-training acceptance check. The decision conflates pre-training dataset validation (K-02, valid) with post-hoc model-quality eval, leaving the central guarantee ('no training until D green via a real metric') unfulfillable as architected.

red_team_findings.what: Cluster D cannot actually be confirmed 'green' because its decision boundary is undefined. The green/red mAP threshold is listed as an open question, and the held-out fixture's ground-truth ownership/labeling is unresolved. If that fixture is labeled by the same detector that generates the pipeline data, the mAP eval is circular and measures nothing.
red_team_findings.why: success_tests require 'FINETUNE-GATE confirmed fully functional' and D's definition-of-done is a CI test that distinguishes red from green by mAP — impossible without a defined threshold and independently-verified ground truth. A gate with an undefined threshold gives false confidence, the exact failure mode (false-done 99034ac5) the keystone claims to fix. More broadly, a 'final' decision whose success_tests depend on six still-open questions is not final.

red_team_findings.what: Constraint-1 traceability gap. The clusters cover bugs #1–#17 exactly (A:1/2/12, B:3/7/8/15, C:4/5/6/16/17, D:9/10/11, E:13/14 = 17), but the three already-committed fixes (771b8dd, 050cb4c, a83b983) are never mapped to any bug number.
red_team_findings.why: Either those commits fixed some of #1–17 — in which case the 23 atoms re-do committed work, violating 'Do not re-do fixes already committed' — or there were really 20 bugs, in which case the '17' accounting is wrong. The task text is itself contradictory ('17 verified' vs 'remaining 17' after 3 fixed: 17−3≠17), and the decision never reconciles it, risking either duplicated effort or a silently dropped bug.

red_team_findings.what: A-FS-01 contradicts the audit's own prescribed fix on an unconfirmed premise. The audit fix is literally 'cut from the event frame = pending.frames[0]', but A-FS-01 rejects frames[0] as wrong-when-a-pre-event-ring-buffer-exists — while whether that buffer exists is an explicit open question.
red_team_findings.why: The canonical event-frame index is therefore unknown, yet the red-first test asserts 'source index != frames[0] when a pre-event buffer is present'. If there is no pre-event buffer, frames[0] is correct and the test encodes the wrong invariant; the fix could be off-by-buffer in either direction. Building the regression test (and TDD red-first proof) on an unverified buffer model can lock in an incorrect fix that still passes its own test.

red_team_findings.what: No handling of already-collected data or the fresh-data dependency K-01 creates. Demoting crops to non-training artifacts invalidates every previously collected sample as a training image; the first run now requires re-collecting enough FULL-FRAME events from scratch.
red_team_findings.why: The risk note only mentions 'reroute plumbing / larger storage', not that the existing dataset is discarded and the first training is gated on new data volume. Combined with E-ML-02's fail-closed quarantine (which drops samples whenever the VLM is unavailable), the positive training set can be starved, delaying or degrading the first training well beyond the bug-fix work itself — an unbudgeted schedule and quality risk for a 'critical' goal.

red_team_findings.what: The artifact the contract names as the single source of truth — bridge-projects/oko/AUDIT_FINDINGS_2026-06-24.md — and the oko code are absent from the working tree where the decision is made; only channels/oko orchestration records exist.
red_team_findings.why: None of the file:line locations, the 'verified' status, the proposed fixes, the three committed SHAs, or 'pytest project oko' can be validated from the available repository. For a critical-risk decomposition, every Judge-accept score and fix claim is unverifiable against real code, and the success_test 'all pytest for project oko pass' is not executable in this context.
